the mass-spectrometrical fragmentation of 1,3- oxazine-4, 6-diones is determined by the nature of the substituents in the 4-position of the oxazine ring and the presence of the 2-aryl substituent.

in the gas-phase 2-aryl-substituted 1,3- oxazine-4, 6-diones exist as a mixture of 4-hydrxy, 6-keto, dicarbonyl, and dipolar-ionic forms, the amounts of the last two forms being increased in the series of derivatives with increasing electron-accepting properties of the aryl group.

the mass spectra of 2-phenyl- and 2-(4-methoxyphenyl)-1,3- oxazine-4, 6-dione in the electron-impact ionization mode are similar to each other and differ from the spectra of 2-(4- nitrophenyl)-1-3-oxazine -4,6-dione.
